This device has no file picker. Open the document from a file manager or share it to Arca.
Nothing to check: the other app did not send a file.
Arca only opens files that the system hands over (content or file addresses).

Choose a document. Arca inspects it inside an isolated sandbox that has no access to your files, network or other apps, shows what is hidden in it, and displays a safe preview as plain text. Nothing in the document is ever run.
You can also drop a file onto this window or share it to Arca from another app.
This app has no network permission. Documents never leave your device.
Arca is free software made by people who ask for nothing in return but support. See who they are and how to help.
The document is only read as data in an isolated sandbox. Nothing in it is opened, run or loaded from the network.
The file is bigger than the limit that keeps the sandbox safe on this device.
The limit on this device is %1$d MiB.
Checking this file exceeded its time limit. A file that is built to waste time is itself a sign of attack. It was stopped and nothing was opened.
The file is damaged or built in a way that no honest program produces. It was refused before any of it was interpreted.
Arca does not know how to read this kind of file, so it shows nothing from it. The file has not been opened or run.
The content is protected by a password, so it cannot be inspected without it. Arca asks for a password only to open the file inside its sandbox; it never keeps it and never tries to guess it.
The password does not open this document. Nothing was opened.
If you know the password, Arca opens the file inside its sandbox and checks what is in it. The password is used once, kept only in memory and wiped when you close the document.
Opening the document and checking what is inside…
That password does not open the document. Try again.
Opened with your password inside the sandbox. Everything below is about the decrypted content; the hash is that of the file you hold.
This file is locked only against editing or copying; it opens without a password, and was opened that way inside the sandbox.
The file tried to use more memory or processing than the sandbox allows (a decompression bomb, for example). It was stopped safely.
Could not read or write the file
The system refused the access or the storage is not available. Try again, or pick the file in a different way.
The app that provided the file did not let Arca read it. Pick the file again with the Open button.
There is nothing in this file to check.
The isolated engine did not start, so no document can be checked safely. Nothing was opened. See Diagnostics for the reason.
An unexpected error stopped the check. The document was not opened and nothing was run.
The picture could not be decoded: it is damaged or built in a way that no picture program produces. Nothing of it was shown.
Grey italic text was composed by Arca from the data of the file (for example a rebuilt SQL query or a link between shapes). It is not text of the document.
No macros, remote content, hidden trackers or other active parts were found in this document.
The document would contact other servers, or carry hidden data about you, when opened in a regular program. Arca does neither.
The document contains parts that run code or take actions (macros, objects, scripts). In Arca none of them can run.
The file is built to exploit programs or to hide its content. Nothing was interpreted. Do not open it elsewhere.
Part of the document could not be inspected, so a clean result cannot be promised. Treat it as untrusted.
A rejected file is not displayed.
A preview is not available for this format.
A rejected file cannot be rebuilt.
A sterile copy is not available for this format.
The source of every macro is shown as text for you to read. It cannot run here.
Runs on its own when the document opens
Addresses and commands in the code
The source is long, so only the beginning is shown.
Addresses the document refers to. Arca never follows them. Tap one to read it in full.

Details about who made the document and how. Documents often carry names, paths and machine names that you may not want to share.
Files and objects stored inside the document. They are listed, never opened.
Numbers from the inspection, useful for a bug report.
Made by Arca. The document was inspected in an isolated sandbox and was not opened or run.
Show only the rows that match
Some pages could not be read
No bookmarks yet. They are kept only while the document is open.
Only the first %1$d headings are listed.
The document is very long, so only the first part is shown.
Nothing to show in this part.
There is nothing to show in this document.
Arca rebuilds the document from its safe parts only and checks the result again. The copy opens in any program without macros, remote content or other active parts.
Macros and scripts, embedded and linked objects, ActiveX, remote templates and images, links that load by themselves, data connections, DDE and risky formulas, and anything the container hides.

All metadata (where and when it was taken, the camera and its serial number, the author), the embedded thumbnail, colour profile and comments, every frame of an animation but the first, and anything stored after the picture.

The copy is a new PNG written from the picture’s pixels alone, so nothing of the original file’s structure survives. A photograph can become larger than its JPEG, a picture of more than 4 megapixels is reduced (unless you keep the full size), an animation keeps only its first frame, and colours are shown as sRGB.

A PDF is rebuilt from its pages: text, pictures and fonts stay exactly as they are. Bookmarks, links, attachments, forms, signatures and old revisions do not; the look of form fields and stamps stays as part of the page.

The copy is a new .docx, .xlsx or .pptx written from the text, tables and pictures the viewer shows: macros, embedded objects, fields, forms and the old file’s hidden data have nowhere to come from. Complex layout (columns, floating shapes, charts) is simplified.
Embedded objects (including charts), thumbnails and signatures are removed from OpenDocument files.
Names, company, paths, printer and editing history.
Hidden data blocks that other programs attach to the document.
Off: a picture of more than 4 megapixels is reduced (a 12-megapixel photo becomes 3), which takes seconds. On: up to 16 megapixels are kept, which takes minutes on a phone.
Remarks of reviewers. The text of the document is not changed.
Deleted text disappears and inserted text becomes normal text. This changes the document.
The original file is never changed. The copy is saved only where you choose.
Then it is inspected again before you can save it.
It was inspected again: no active content, remote content or hidden trackers remain.
The copy could not be fully verified
It was rebuilt without the dangerous parts, but part of it could not be inspected again. Open it with care.

Translucent glossy panels over a soft colour wash. Off by default; turning it on changes only how the app looks.
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
Hides the app in the recent-apps list and stops screenshots and screen recording. Turn off if you need to capture the screen.
Hidden text, sheets and slides appear in the preview marked as hidden. They can always be toggled there.

Pictures inside documents are decoded in the sandbox only when you tap them. Turn on to show them as soon as a document opens.
Arca is free and has no ads. If it helps you, you can support the developers.
That PDF could have been carrying a zero-day exploit, but it died quietly inside our air-gapped Wasm sandbox. Buy our digital bomb squad a coffee!
Just like legendary WinRAR: we will never lock features behind a paywall or nag you into a subscription. But tossing a coin to your SecOps engineers grants +1000 karma.
Good news: the sketchy macro in that spreadsheet was neutralized. Bad news: the developers are running dangerously low on espresso. Care to refuel the tank?
Arca requests exactly ZERO permissions from your OS. We don’t even know who you are—and we like it that way. Support truly private open-source software!
While mainstream office suites phone home to thirty ad-tech servers before rendering a comma, we don’t even have the INTERNET permission. Keep independent code alive!
Zero tracking pixels got through. Whoever sent you that document still has no idea if you opened it. Consider us your personal digital alibi.
Built in 100%% memory-safe Rust with zero legacy C/C++ parsers. Because buffer overflows belong in history books, not on your phone. Support paranoid engineering!
Opening mysterious attachments from group chats is an extreme sport. Opening them in Arca is just Tuesday. Chip in to keep the strongbox evolving!
Our engineers are so paranoid that the host doesn’t even trust its own sandbox’s output. Help us fund our next batch of titanium-grade tinfoil hats.
Another week, zero successful exploits! If Arca saved your sanity (or your device) recently, consider visiting our support page.
You just inspected a relational Access database on a mobile phone without uploading a single byte to the cloud. In the Middle Ages that was witchcraft; today it’s FOSS!
White-on-white text? VeryHidden spreadsheet tabs? Nothing escapes the Threat X-Ray. If you appreciate forensic clarity, support the team behind it.
0%% ads, 0%% analytics, 0%% venture capital strings attached, 100%% respect for your sovereignty. Arca thrives solely on community patronage.
If office documents could talk, half of them would be reading your metadata to data brokers. We politely put them in a soundproof Wasm room.
Our One-Tap Sterile Copy leaves documents cleaner than a Swiss operating theater: zero author trails, zero printer paths, zero hidden revisions.
We can’t sell your data even if someone offered us a billion dollars—because we literally never collect it. Our only business model is building great security tools.
A 100:1 decompression zip bomb? That’s just a light morning stretch for our fuel-metered sandbox. Support the shield that guards your RAM!
Notice how quiet it is in here? No pop-up ads, no dark-pattern upsells, no background telemetry daemons. If you value digital peace, support Pharos.
Even if someone sends you a haunted binary document straight out of 1998, we’ll dissect it safely without letting a single byte touch system decoders.
Standard office app: “Let’s fetch this remote template over SMB!” Arca: “Nobody moves, drop the NTLM hash and step away from the socket!” Support your pocket firewall.
This weekly note is gentler than a cat asking for breakfast at 6 AM. No paywalls, no guilt trips—just an honest link if you’d like to back the project.
We ditched bloated third-party UI frameworks and wrote our own dependency-free stack so supply-chain attacks have nowhere to hide. Handcrafted security takes love!
What you read is strictly your business. We don’t log your activity timeline or study your behavior inside the app. Pure zero-trust viewing, zero strings attached.
Visio diagrams, spreadsheets, slide decks, and databases—all rendered inside an air-gapped vault. Help us forge even stronger walls for the next release!
Exploit brokers pay millions for image and font parser bugs. We decode pixels in safe Rust inside WebAssembly so they can cry into their keyboards instead.
No “Pro Tier”, no artificial limits, no fine print. Every security feature in Arca is free forever, because safety shouldn’t be a luxury.
They say bug-free software is a myth, but software stripped of network sockets, filesystem access, and system calls comes pretty darn close.
Forensic scan complete: this app contains 100%% independent engineering and 0%% corporate surveillance. Fuel the FOSS rebellion!
Every donation to the Pharos team is deterministically compiled into stricter fuzzing harnesses, faster parsers, and cleaner page rendering.
You trust Arca to inspect your riskiest files; we trust the community to keep this project independent. Thank you for standing with open-source security!
True Zero-Trust: Arca has no internet access, collects zero telemetry, never studies or logs your in-app behavior, and sells zero ads. We build this solely to keep you safe.
Show a non-intrusive card once every 7 days on the home screen
Nothing counted yet. Open a document and the numbers will appear here.
These totals are counted and kept only on this device, with no dates and no history. They are never sent anywhere, and no file names or contents are stored.

Off by default, so Arca leaves no trace of what you open. When you turn it on, Arca keeps a few flat all-time totals on this device: documents opened, dangerous software and trackers neutralised, files rejected, sterile copies. No dates, no times, no history by day. Turning it off deletes the totals at once.
The totals stored on this device are erased at once and cannot be restored. Your documents are not affected.
Tap an entry to see the full address first. Nothing is copied or opened until you choose to. After pasting an address, compare its beginning and its end with the one shown here.
The copied address is removed from the clipboard after one minute where the system allows it.
